Regional consumption and import data used to estimate domestic total availability and import reliance. • In 2024, North America deployed over 120,000 high-voltage circuit breakers led by U.S. substation upgrades and smart grid projects across California and Texas.43 - Data on domestic manufacturing output or imports for high-voltage breakers not available from public data sources - Facility-specific output number to estimate of breaker output based on employee numbers or factory size also not available from public data sources • Assume 25-75% of units consumed each year in the U.S. are imported - Import data for lower-voltage circuit breakers over 1000 V but less than 72.5 kV* showed that over the 2016 – 2020 period, import shares ranged from 75% to 26% based on number of units44 - We assume the fraction of imports for high-voltage circuit breakers have a similar range, 75% - 25% * Based on HS codes: 853521; 853529 National Laboratory of the Rockies | 25 Annual Circuit Breaker Availability U.S. annual production capability and access to over 120,000 high-voltage circuit breakers. • Assume 25-75% of units imported (Photo by Dennis Schroeder / NLR) Availability Assumptions Availability Assumptions National Laboratory of the Rockies | 26 Towers Towers • The average high-voltage transmission tower includes about 40-60k lb. of steel45 • There are many manufacturers of high voltage transmission towers46 • Given the numerous manufacturers, we assume constraints for transmission towers are driven by steel availability and not manufacturing technology/capability Photo by Warren Gretz / NLR Annual Transmission Tower Availability Transmission tower manufacturing capacity is unconstrained.
